## Odessa consular routing and a Magdeburg wagon-sale instruction

**Sources on this page:** p201 A1, p201 A2.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-odessa-wagon-sale-odessa-consular-routing-and-a-magdeburg-wagon-sale-instruction"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two native parts give the consular and export-company routing of an instruction involving the sale of a railway wagon. The primary edition retains the opaque DAMM LADWIG phrase and all incomplete references. More fluent cargo-word proposals are priced separately rather than silently treated as source wording.

<a id="source-p201-a1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-finance-odessa-wagon-sale-p201-a1"></a>

### p201 A1

**Source transcription — header:** `A) NKJ FUER RAT (6.50 a.m., November 16th); 0700 (16) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-254`

Under the [existing November date constraint](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md),
the opening reference becomes **Nr. 8?**, raising the conditional reading
to **125/127** positions. The other reference cells remain distinct and
unassigned; no source coordinate changes.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
DEUTSCHESGENERALKONSULATODESSAXNRX??XAUSSENUKRAANDEUTSCHEENBEVOLLMAECHTIGTENODESSAXFUERAUSFUHRGESELLSCHAFTXABTXRMX?IHRTELEGRAMM
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> Deutsches Generalkonsulat Odessa. Nr. ?? AUSSENUKRA. An DEUTSCHEEN Bevollmaechtigten Odessa. Fuer Ausfuhrgesellschaft. Abt. RM ? Ihr Telegramm

**Meaning:** The first part gives the German consulate at Odessa, an unresolved numbered reference, the Odessa representative and an export company as address or routing information. It then begins a reference to a previous telegram. The spelling DEUTSCHEEN and AUSSENUKRA are retained without silently normalizing them.

**Editorial limits:**

- All 254 coordinates are present in the printed source and decode without repair. The earlier OCR split the first row from the rest; the complete native body is now used.
- DEUTSCHEEN is retained with both E letters. AUSSENUKRA, ABT and RM remain unexpanded, and RM is not treated as a currency amount.
- The baseline question marks use three different cells, FD, GF and GD. The conditional layer fixes FD=8; GF and GD retain distinct values from `034679`.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-odessa-wagon-sale-p201-a2"></a>

### p201 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) NKJ FUER RAT (6.50 a.m., November 16th); 0700 (16) 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-236`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
?WEITAUSENDUNDACHTZIGERSUCHENWAGGONMAGDEBURGNEUNTAUSENDNEUNHUNDERTZEHNXDAMMXLADWIGBESTMOEGLICHSTZUVERKAUFENXAUSWAERTIG
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ZWEITAUSENDUNDACHTZIGERSUCHENWAGGONMAGDEBURGNEUNTAUSENDNEUNHUNDERTZEHNXDAMMXLADWIGBESTMOEGLICHSTZUVERKAUFENXAUSWAERTIG
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Zweitausendundachtzig. Ersuchen Waggon Magdeburg neuntausendneunhundertzehn. DAMM LADWIG bestmoeglichst zu verkaufen. Auswaertig.

**Meaning:** The continuation refers to the telegram with the spelled-out number zweitausendundachtzig and requests a sale on the best possible terms involving the wagon identified by Magdeburg and neuntausendneunhundertzehn. DAMM LADWIG remains opaque in the primary edition; it is not treated as a confirmed person, cargo description or instruction to sell the contents.

**Editorial limits:**

- The native 236-coordinate body is preserved. The initial unresolved square label is changed to Z in ZWEITAUSEND as one observed-coordinate substitution; this is not a free fill of an unknown square cell.
- Both long numbers remain spelled out exactly as recovered. No wagon identity is independently established from those words.
- The primary reading retains DAMM LADWIG. Conditional LADUNG, SAMT LADUNG and DANN LADUNG alternatives are separately priced, and none is silently substituted into the primary meaning.
- SAMT LADUNG and DANN LADUNG each require nine observed changes from the source, including the initial Z proposal; coordinate cost alone does not choose between them.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-odessa-wagon-sale-conditional-interpretation-cargo-wording"></a>

### Conditional interpretation: cargo wording

The primary reading leaves DAMM LADWIG unresolved. Replacing LADWIG with LADUNG would make a cargo reading possible, but costs four further observed-coordinate changes. The longer phrase SAMT LADUNG would suggest selling the wagon together with its load; DANN LADUNG is an equally costly alternative under the same coordinate metric. These are proposals, not independent source recoveries.

| Phrase retained or proposed | Total observed substitutions from the native source, including initial Z | Additional substitutions beyond the primary edition |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DAMM LADWIG — primary | 1 | 0 |
| DAMM LADUNG | 5 | 4 |
| SAMT LADUNG | 9 | 8 |
| DANN LADUNG | 9 | 8 |

All three conditional streams and their exact coordinate edits re-encrypt under the unchanged published key. Equal cost does not select the historical phrase. The edition therefore does not present the sale of the wagon’s contents as established. The spelled-out references remain the source’s words; neither consular routing nor a plausible commercial sentence identifies the particular wagon independently.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-odessa-wagon-sale-evidence-credit-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/odessa_wagon_sale/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

## p201 B / p206 A — reporting orders linked by a shared reference

**Sources on this page:** p201 B1, p201 B2.

**Related source pages:** [p206 A1](206.md#source-p206-a1), [p206 A2](206.md#source-p206-a2), [p206 A3](206.md#source-p206-a3).

<a id="edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders-p201-b--p206-a--reporting-orders-linked-by-a-shared-reference"></a>



**Status:** Two complete multipart messages are assembled from the source:
a two-part reporting order on p201 and a three-part request for receipt
confirmation on p206. The unchanged published `Nov16-18` partial key fixes
**660 of 702 plaintext positions** from **1,404 source coordinate slots**.
Their matching number pattern and subject support a **conditional new digit

**Source assembly and analysis:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Period-key

<a id="edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders-reporting-order-on-p201"></a>

### Reporting order on p201

**Readable German — body excerpt; the unresolved closing reference remains in the raw output below:**

> Erreichte Ziele regelmaessig hierher melden, desgl. wo u. wann ersten
> Teile voraussichtlich die deutsche Grenze erreichen werden, ob mit
> Bahn/Fussmarsch und welche Teile des sind. Empfang bestaetigen. OHL.

**Meaning:** Report reached positions regularly, and say where and when the
first units are expected to reach the German border, whether by rail or on
foot, and which units they are. Acknowledge receipt.

The source has the awkward `ERSTEN` and `DESSIND`; both are retained in the
German reading above. No final `N` is dropped to regularize the former.
The English translation conveys the sentence's apparent meaning
without claiming that its spelling is recovered differently. `WERD?N` is
shown as `werden` using one explicitly costed source-coordinate correction.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders-the-three-part-confirmation-request-on-p206"></a>

### The three-part confirmation request on p206

The later message asks OKM to confirm immediately whether seven earlier
orders arrived. It identifies the subject of each: the departure order,
reporting intentions, destructions, refusal to surrender weapons,
negotiations with Romania, the armistice, and reporting reached positions.
It then demands immediate reports of the divisions' locations and
acknowledgment of the present order.

The [p206 source](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p206_selected.png)
has an **18 November** heading and internal stamp but a **19 November** receipt:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
ZON v LP (06.28 a.m., November 19th)
2100 (11/18) 3 TEILE
1 TL: RICHI-368
2 TL: RICHI-400
3 TL: RICHI-248
```

</details>

The first OCR block ended after 40 coordinates, before the printed `RICHI`
label. Rejoining the two visually continuous source rows restores the
complete 368-slot first part. The third part has exactly its stated 248
slots; the earlier OCR's extra character is not part of the printed source.
These are transcription/layout corrections, not hypothetical historical
insertions or deletions.

| Part | Source slots | Directly fixed plaintext | Separately proposed body repairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| A1 | 368 | 175/184 | Two erasure fills in `BETR` and `BEFEHL`. |
| A2 | 400 | 179/200 | Six erasure fills in words/separators; one erased coordinate in a number remains unresolved. |
| A3 | 248 | 115/124 | Four erasure fills; two known-coordinate substitutions for `DMR→DER` and `EXPFANG→EMPFANG`. |

The first part retains an overtyped, unclear coordinate as `?`; visible dashes
remain erasures. The third part's repeated `BEFEHLSBEFEHLS` is retained rather
than silently shortened. Its final reference begins with a directly decoded
`J`; this is not replaced with a guessed `1`.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders-the-shared-reference-and-conditional-digit-5"></a>

### The shared reference and conditional digit 5

The p201 order ends with the number `11??2`. The seventh p206 reference also
has `11??2`, followed by the subject `BEFEHL ERREICHTE ZIELE MELDEN`.
Their number is identical at the square-cell level:

| Position in five-character reference | p201 B2 digraph | p206 A2 digraph | Published-key reading |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 0 | VX | VX | 1 |
| 1 | VX | VX | 1 |
| 2 | FA | FA | ? |
| 3 | VV | VV | ? |
| 4 | DV | DV | 2 |

The unknown number positions are therefore shared variables, not four
independent guesses. The matching body subject further supports identifying
the seventh reference with the p201 order.

The referenced date on p206 is `1{VA}.11`. If the clear p201 origin stamp
`OHL OP 15/11` is the date of that same order, **VA must contain 5**.
This assigns zero-based square cell **24**. It changes no source coordinate
and is independent of the [p204 calendar inference](204.md#edition-cases-radio-p204-a).

The link remains conditional on the identification of the order and the
correct copying of its date and reference. An equal partly unknown number
alone would not prove that two documents concern the same order; the matching
subject and explicit source date are why the inference is recorded here.
No unrestricted completion of the remaining square cells is claimed.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders-reference-list-under-the-two-explicit-inferences"></a>

### Reference list under the two explicit inferences

The following display applies **VA = 5** from the order link and **FD = 8**
from p204's Monday date. Other unknown cells and erasures stay unknown:

| Reference | Conditional number | Conditional date | Directly readable subject |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `11212` | `?.11` | `ABMARSCHBEFEHL` — departure order |
| 2 | `1125?` | `?.11` | `BEFEHL ABSICHTEN ZU MELDEN` — report intentions |
| 3 | `11?2?` | `8.11` | `ZERSTOERUNGEN` — destructions |
| 4 | `11???` | `8.11` | `ABLEHNUNG DER WAFFENABGABE` — refusal to surrender weapons |
| 5 | `11???` | `8.11` | `VERHANDLUNGEN MIT RUMAENIEN` — negotiations with Romania |
| 6 | `11???` | `1?.11` | `WAFFENSTILLSTAND` — armistice |
| 7 | `11??2` | `15.11` | `BEFEHL ERREICHTE ZIELE MELDEN` — report reached positions |

The date order in this list is not used as an additional constraint. The
other serial numbers are not forced into an assumed numerical sequence.

Across p204 and the three p206 parts, the two assignments jointly add **seven
fixed positions** under the stated assumptions. They also fix exactly one
position in the separately audited [p205 financial message](205.md#edition-cases-finance-p205-a):
part A4's plaintext index **86** becomes `5`, turning `NRX1???STRICH11` into
`NRX1??5STRICH11`. The p205 source package and base reading remain unchanged.
Its other unknown reference cells then share the remaining digit domain
`034679`; they are not independently chosen.

## p201 C — Courier Elsner, arrival via Wilna and an inquiry about further couriers

**Edition context:** Odessa courier report: a conditional loss before transposition.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-odessa-courier-pretransposition-odessa-courier-report-a-conditional-loss-before-transposition"></a>



The conditional reconstruction of p201 C reports courier Elsner’s arrival via Wilna and asks whether further couriers should leave for Odessa. The clear header dates the Berlin telegram to **15 November 1918**. The recovered body now fixes **161/163 positions**; two reference labels remain unresolved.

Research and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The published Nov16–18 key retains the credit of George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker; the [same-page address witness](#edition-cases-finance-odessa-wagon-sale-p201-a1) retains its earlier body credit.

### Current conditional reading

**Readable German — both retained loss models, the existing word repairs and shared FD=8 / VA=5 conditions:**

> Deutschen Bevollmaechtigten Odessa. Kurier Elsner heute ueber Wilna hier eingetroffen. Sollen Kuriere nach dort noch abfahren. Verbind. Offz. O Roem 2 der O. H. L. Berlin. ZT? Nr. 1?1118.

**Meaning:** Elsner has arrived via Wilna. The sender asks whether further couriers are still to depart for Odessa. The liaison-officer closing and Berlin remain literal; the report does not establish Elsner’s full identity.

The reading uses the existing two-coordinate loss model before transposition, two added fractionation fills and four observed-coordinate word repairs. The **324 received coordinates** remain in their printed order. The existing [FD=8 / VA=5 interpretation](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md) supplies the final **8** without another source edit: the pair is **FD**, at received positions **187** and **289**. It survives both loss descriptions, **[36, 74]** and **[37, 74]**, and the conservative **G??DV** branch, which fixes **159/163 positions**.

The remaining reference cells **AF** and **GG** take distinct values from **034679**. The [propagation certificate](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/courier_certificate.json) retains all **30** reference tuples and **720** complete square assignments, with the original **324-coordinate transposition** and **326-coordinate fractionation**.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-odessa-courier-pretransposition-what-the-two-loss-model-means"></a>

### The two-loss fractionation model

All indices below are zero-based. The inverse column permutation always has length **324**. Its output is a 324-coordinate intermediate stream. The proposed original fractionated stream has length **326**, with missing positions **36 and 74**. Inserting **X** and **A** there makes complete plaintext pairs.

The forward check is equally explicit:

1. Fractionate the proposed 163-label plaintext into 326 coordinates.
2. Remove the coordinates at the stated two fractionation positions.
3. Apply the published column permutation to the remaining **324** coordinates.

Before the later word repairs, this process reproduces the entire native received source exactly. After those repairs it reproduces a 324-slot received stream differing from the source at precisely the four disclosed indices. Applying a 326-coordinate column permutation would be a different model and is not used here.

The first missing X can be described at position **36 or 37**, next to the same observed X. Both descriptions produce the same filled fractionated stream. They retain different origin maps and different unfilled pair domains; neither alias is selected as the historical location.

<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>


</details>

This unfilled model fixes **157/163 positions**. The restored pair boundaries already expose most of the address and courier wording. Its two question marks at the inserted coordinates remain source absences rather than observed values.

**Conditional interpretation — same fractionation frame after the two explicit X/A fills, before the four ordinary-word repairs:**

<a id="edition-cases-radio-odessa-courier-pretransposition-bounded-placement-evidence"></a>

### Bounded placement evidence

The search uses five retrospective prefix spans at fixed offsets: DEUTSCHEN, BEVOLLMAECHTIGTEN, ODESSA, KURIER and ELSNER. It compares every pair of missing positions in a 326-coordinate fractionated stream with the **unchanged 324-coordinate intermediate source**. All **52,975** pairs are priced in each scope. The objective counts conflicts with observed coordinates; inserted values are separately supplied from the chosen word stencil.

| Retrospective word scope | Minimum observed changes | All tied missing-position pairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All five prefix spans | 0 | 2 |
| ODESSA omitted | 0 | 2 |
| Address words only | 0 | 522 |
| KURIER omitted | 0 | 32 |

The first two scopes retain exactly **[36,74] and [37,74]**. ODESSA therefore appears without being forced by that second stencil. The broader address-only and courier-omitted minima remain in full; they show what depends on the selected courier vocabulary. These are sensitivity checks after the reading was seen, not blind predictions.

Repeating the same scans with both overstruck source glyphs masked leaves the same minimum sets. That protects the geometry comparison from choosing the X readings through the prefix words. Completing the two glyph masks as X would nevertheless be two additional mask fills in that conservative branch.

The existing p201 A1 body directly reads **BEVOLLMAECHTIGTEN** followed by **ODESSA**, with complete observed pairs. Its exact source indices are rechecked in the certificate. This independently attests the recipient vocabulary. It is not an identical courier report and supplies no name, travel route, date or reference number to this body.

| 227 | D | A | HEUTBBEBER → HEUTEUEBER |

<a id="edition-cases-radio-odessa-courier-pretransposition-reference-labels-and-exact-reproduction"></a>

### Reference labels and exact reproduction

Under the earlier baseline square, the three remaining primary unknowns occur at plaintext positions **152, 157 and 161**, from the distinct square cells **AF, GG and FD**. Each has the individual domain **0,3,4,5,6,7,8,9**. Because the square is one-to-one, their three labels must be distinct. The literal known 1s and ROEM 2 do not select the missing labels.

The earlier baseline check retains all **40,320** assignments to the eight unknown square cells with the forward loss-before-transposition process. They yield **336 distinct ordered reference triples**. One full-square witness for every triple is retained. These are proofs of alternatives, not historical choices of a date, serial or telegram number.

| Quantity | Earlier baseline edition |
| --- | ---: |
| Native received slots / advertised slots | 324 / 324 |
| Received transposition length | 324 |
| Reconstructed fractionation length | 326 |
| Plaintext positions | 163 |

| Unfilled loss-model fixed positions | 157/163 |

| Received source insertions / exclusions | 0 / 0 |

[The portable verifier](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/verify.py) binds the native source, both origin maps, all placement minima and cost-distribution hashes, every word repair, the conservative glyph branch, the live complete displays, the independent address-word pairs and all global reference alternatives. [The certificate](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/certificates.json) contains the complete evidence. [The frozen OCR record](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/ocr_snapshot.json) preserves the earlier incomplete transcription.

```sh
python experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/verify.py --verify
python experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
python experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/verify_courier.py --verify
```

The exact forward reproduction establishes the arithmetic of the proposed model. It does not authenticate a historical omission mechanism, replace the native reading, or prove global optimality over other keys and error models.
